The problem is pure bending of a rectangular cross-section beam; no shear force, axial force, or torsion acts on the section of interest.
The material is linearly elastic and deformations are small, so the classical Euler-Bernoulli bending theory applies and plane sections remain plane.
The internal bending moment at the section is M = 4,000,000 N·mm, positive (sagging).
The cross-section is rectangular with width b = 50 mm and height h = 120 mm.
The moment of inertia about the centroidal (neutral) axis is I = b·h³/12 = 50·120³/12 = 7,200,000 mm⁴.
The coordinate y is measured from the neutral axis (centroid), positive upward.
The governing relation for normal bending stress is σ = −M·y / I.
Compute σ at three fiber locations:
At y = 0 mm (neutral axis): σ = 0 MPa.
At y = +60 mm (top fiber): σ = −(4,000,000·60)/7,200,000 = −33.33 MPa (compression).
At y = −60 mm (bottom fiber): σ = −(4,000,000·(−60))/7,200,000 = +33.33 MPa (tension).
All results are reported in MPa using the N–mm unit system.
No additional assumptions beyond those stated are required.
